# Continual-ARC solved rule: recolor complete uniform grid lines (task-c25b713c)

**Verified by correct test submission with zero wrong attempts.**

## Rule

Find any row or column that is entirely the same color (the line color). Recolor every cell belonging to each such complete row or column to color `2`. Preserve all other cells exactly as they were. If a cell belongs to both a qualifying row and column, it is still simply `2`.

The complete line color varies by instance; do not assume a particular input color. A line must span the full grid dimension. Do not recolor partial stripes or scattered cells of that color merely because they match the line color.

## Evidence from demonstrations

- Demo 1 (21x28): background `1`, line color `1`. Complete rows and columns are changed to `2`; other cells, including non-line `1`s and the scattered `3`s, remain unchanged.
- Demo 2 (22x13): background `9`, line color `3`. Entire column 8 and full rows 6, 14, 18, and 19 (zero-based) are recolored to `2`; partial `3` groups elsewhere remain unchanged.

## Confirmed test

Input was 12x8 with full columns 2 and 3 and full row 9, all color `5`. Correct output changed just those two columns and that row to `2`, preserving every other input cell (including other `5`s). Evaluator confirmed correct.

## Additional verified instance (2026-10-20; one demonstration)

- Demo input/output: 24x4, with one fully uniform column (zero-based column 1, all `9`) and three fully uniform rows (zero-based rows 2, 19, and 21, all `9`). Those entire lines became `2`; all other cells were unchanged, including scattered `9`s not on complete lines.
- Test input/output: 26x23, confirmed correct by evaluator after one incorrect submission. The complete uniform lines were rows 9 and 25, and columns 9, 15, 18, and 22 (zero-based), all `9`. Recolor the union of these lines to `2`; preserve all other cells. This independently reconfirms that detection checks full rows/columns, not just rows or the most common/background color.
- A guess recoloring only the two full rows was incorrect; make sure to inspect columns too. The successful output changed all cells in the four full columns and two full rows to `2`, and nothing else.

## Application checklist

1. Inspect each row and column for a single repeated value across its entire length.
2. Mark all qualifying rows and columns before modifying anything.
3. Set their union of cells to `2`; leave all cells outside that union unchanged.
4. Keep the original grid dimensions.

## Additional verified instance (2026-10-20; task-c25b713c)

A demo and the test independently confirm the same rule: recolor the union of every fully uniform row and every fully uniform column to `2`; preserve all cells outside those full lines, including isolated/partial cells that happen to match the line color.

- Demo 1: 22x20 grid, line color `3`. The fully uniform lines were row 6 and columns 0, 14, and 15 (zero-based); those became `2`. Partial/scattered `3`s elsewhere remained `3`.
- Test: 9x26 grid, line color `6`. Fully uniform rows were 2 and 8; fully uniform columns were 3, 9, 13, 16, 21, and 25 (zero-based). Their union became `2`. Other `6`s, such as at (row 3, col 18), (row 5, col 4), and (row 6, col 11), remained unchanged. Evaluator confirmed the output correct after one incorrect attempt.

For future instances, scan all rows and columns, mark only those whose entire length is one repeated value, then recolor their union to `2`. Do not infer that every occurrence of the separator color belongs to a full line.
